stats.no_fit_reason: This is fundamentally a physical maintenance process. The core pain points—hands-on equipment inspection, hands-on repair work, and physical parts delivery—are not information-processing problems that AI can solve. While maintenance logs and parts inventory are data artifacts of the process, the actual value delivery (detecting wear, performing repairs, stocking parts) depends on technician expertise and physical work. AI might support peripheral tasks like scheduling optimization or inventory forecasting, but those are not among the named pain points, and adding a tool that does not address the stated problems would be padding. The process is not a good AI candidate.

process: Annual performance review drafting and calibration

stats.no_fit_reason: This process involves evaluation of worker performance and behavior, and decisions about employment continuation and development — it falls squarely into the EU AI Act HIGH-risk category (Annex III, recitals on worker evaluation and promotion/termination decisions). Any AI assistance in drafting or calibrating performance reviews risks automating a decision that must remain fully human, transparent, and contestable by the employee. The pain points (varying write-up quality, calibration preparation burden) are real, but they are best addressed through better manager training, templates, and structured review frameworks — not AI automation. Using AI to synthesize, score, or recommend performance judgments on workers creates unacceptable legal, ethical, and adoption risk: employees have a right to contest their evaluation, and an AI-assisted score could be opaque to them. The sensitivity of the data (employee performance, personal file) combined with the HIGH AI Act risk makes this a clear no-fit for AI intervention.

use_cases.description: An AI tool that extracts and structures key terms from current policy documents and broker quotes (coverage limits, exclusions, deductibles, premium, renewal dates) into a standardized comparison table.
use_cases.justification: This directly addresses the manual quote comparison pain point by automatically extracting comparable fields from multiple broker proposals, reducing the time spent manually cross-referencing unstructured documents and enabling faster, more accurate side-by-side analysis.

criteria_rationale.quality_impact: Consistent extraction of policy terms across documents reduces manual transcription errors and ensures all quotes are compared on the same dimensions.
criteria_rationale.strategic_alignment: Improves procurement efficiency and cost control, though not a top-line revenue driver.
criteria_rationale.data_quality: Policy and quote documents are PDF/text, but formatting varies across brokers; some manual cleanup may be needed.
criteria_rationale.technical_complexity: Specialized document extraction with domain-specific field mapping; moderate complexity but established pattern.
criteria_rationale.adoption_risk: Procurement and finance teams already work with structured data; this reduces their manual pivot-table work with minimal workflow disruption.
criteria_rationale.off_the_shelf: Several insurance quote-aggregation platforms and document-extraction vendors offer this capability.
criteria_rationale.ai_act: Internal procurement document processing; no profiling or regulatory decisions, so minimal risk.
criteria_rationale.gdpr: Processes asset inventory and claims history, but neither contains personal data.

use_cases.description: An AI assistant that retrieves and summarizes key coverage gaps, claim patterns, and risk exposures from the company's claims history and asset inventory, then flags which broker quotes address those gaps, assisting the human decision-maker.
use_cases.justification: This targets the rushed renewal timeline and the need for legal/insurance expertise by automating the analysis of historical claims and risk profile, surfacing which quotes best align with the company's actual loss patterns and asset base, so the finance/procurement team can make a more informed recommendation faster.

criteria_rationale.quality_impact: Systematic review of claims and risk patterns ensures informed renewal decisions and reduces the risk of under-coverage from rushed analysis.
criteria_rationale.strategic_alignment: Reduces renewal risk and improves cost-benefit tradeoffs; a secondary but important operational priority.
criteria_rationale.data_quality: Claims history and asset inventory exist internally but may require normalization; structured enough for analysis once cleaned.
criteria_rationale.technical_complexity: Requires parsing claims data and asset registry, then summarizing risk gaps against quote coverage; custom build, but straightforward NLP and rules.
criteria_rationale.adoption_risk: Procurement and legal review staff remain decision-makers; the tool is advisory, so minimal change to roles.
criteria_rationale.off_the_shelf: No single vendor package maps claims patterns to quote coverage; requires custom integration.
criteria_rationale.ai_act: Internal risk analysis tool; no profiling or automated decisions affecting individuals or external parties.
criteria_rationale.gdpr: Uses only company asset and loss data; no personal data processed.

use_cases.description: A classifier that evaluates product condition photos against return policy eligibility criteria (damage, usage level, restocking requirements) and flags whether the return meets condition thresholds, with agent approval.
use_cases.justification: This directly addresses inconsistent return decisions across agents by applying condition rules consistently to every return request. High volume (4000/month) and 4-minute baseline make automation of repetitive condition assessment valuable.

criteria_rationale.quality_impact: Applies damage/usage thresholds consistently, reducing agent-to-agent variance in eligibility decisions.
criteria_rationale.strategic_alignment: Reduces customer friction and return processing time, supporting revenue retention and customer satisfaction.
criteria_rationale.data_quality: Product condition photos vary in angle, lighting, and customer photography skill; requires moderate training data.
criteria_rationale.technical_complexity: Custom image classification model is needed; condition assessment is moderately complex compared to commodity vision APIs.
criteria_rationale.adoption_risk: Agents still review flagged cases, so workflow remains largely unchanged; low resistance expected.
criteria_rationale.off_the_shelf: General image classifiers exist but product condition assessment is domain-specific; custom training needed.
criteria_rationale.ai_act: Internal customer-facing triage with no profiling of customers; minimal risk category.
criteria_rationale.gdpr: Processes product images and purchase history; indirect personal data (linked to customer order, not customer identity itself).

use_cases.description: An AI assistant that retrieves order history and purchase date from the order management system and cross-references the return policy rules in real-time, surfacing eligibility status (in-window, out-of-window, needs exception) to the agent without requiring manual lookups across multiple systems.
use_cases.justification: This targets the pain point of agents manually checking multiple systems to verify purchase date and eligibility. At 4000 occurrences/month × 4 minutes, with ~1–1.5 minutes spent on cross-system lookups, automation here directly reduces chat handling time.

criteria_rationale.quality_impact: Eliminates manual lookup delays and errors; agents get consistent, real-time eligibility status every time.
criteria_rationale.strategic_alignment: Directly reduces chat handling time and improves customer response speed, supporting operational efficiency and satisfaction.
criteria_rationale.data_quality: Order history and return policy rules are structured, clean, and readily available in existing systems.
criteria_rationale.technical_complexity: API-driven data retrieval and policy rule matching; straightforward integration with existing order and policy systems.
criteria_rationale.adoption_risk: Agents simply receive structured eligibility data instead of querying systems manually; minimal workflow disruption.
criteria_rationale.off_the_shelf: Retrieval-and-summarization assistants are a mature commodity; many platforms offer pre-built integration templates.
criteria_rationale.ai_act: Internal back-office data retrieval and policy matching; no customer profiling or behavior evaluation.
criteria_rationale.gdpr: Accesses order history and customer identity linked to returns; indirect personal data.

use_cases.description: An AI tool that automatically extracts transaction details (date, amount, description, reference codes) from bank statements and general ledger exports, standardizing formats and flagging data quality issues before manual matching begins.
use_cases.justification: This directly addresses the manual burden of processing thousands of transactions by automating the extraction and standardization step, which is currently a significant portion of the 600-minute month-end process. By surfacing data quality issues early, it also reduces the time spent tracing discrepancies later.

criteria_rationale.quality_impact: Standardized extraction reduces manual keying errors and inconsistencies in how transactions are read from PDFs and CSV files.
criteria_rationale.strategic_alignment: Directly supports cost control and compliance (zero-error close deadline) by accelerating a critical month-end control process.
criteria_rationale.data_quality: Bank statements and GL exports are well-structured but arrive in mixed formats (PDF, CSV, text); extraction must handle these variations.
criteria_rationale.technical_complexity: Standard document extraction (OCR for PDFs, structured parsing for CSVs) is a mature, low-risk pattern.
criteria_rationale.adoption_risk: Accountants still review and validate all extracted data; the tool is transparent and inserted early in the workflow.
criteria_rationale.off_the_shelf: Several accounting-specific OCR and document extraction tools already handle bank statement parsing.
criteria_rationale.ai_act: Internal financial reconciliation automation with no personal profiling or regulatory decision-making is minimal risk.
criteria_rationale.gdpr: Processes transaction and bank account data that is indirectly linked to the company, not personal data.

use_cases.description: A classifier that flags matched transaction pairs (bank statement line ↔ GL entry) as high-confidence, low-confidence, or unmatched, to triage which reconciling items need manual investigation versus which are routine and can be cleared quickly.
use_cases.justification: This targets the close deadline pressure and the zero-tolerance requirement by automatically screening routine matches from true discrepancies. Accountants can then focus manual effort only on the flagged anomalies, reducing the time spent on routine verification of thousands of line items.

criteria_rationale.quality_impact: Reduces false positives in anomaly detection, but final approval remains manual; modest consistency gain from applying the same matching logic to all transactions.
criteria_rationale.strategic_alignment: Directly reduces close time and ensures zero-tolerance compliance by expediting the triage of reconciling items — a top priority for month-end controls.
criteria_rationale.data_quality: Extracted transaction data (from first use case) is now structured and comparable; prior workpapers provide labeled examples for model training.
criteria_rationale.technical_complexity: Classification on numeric fields (amount, date) and text similarity is a low-complexity supervised learning task.
criteria_rationale.adoption_risk: Accountants retain manual override authority and final sign-off; tool is an aid to routing, not an autonomous decision maker.
criteria_rationale.off_the_shelf: Several ERP and finance automation vendors (e.g., SAP Concur, BlackLine) offer built-in reconciliation matching modules.
criteria_rationale.ai_act: Internal financial controls with no autonomous approval or personal profiling is minimal risk.
criteria_rationale.gdpr: Uses the same indirectly personal transaction and account data as the extraction step.

use_cases.description: An AI tool that retrieves approved content from the calendar, matches it to platform-specific posting guidelines (LinkedIn, Instagram, Twitter/X, etc.), and generates a pre-filled scheduling form for each platform that the marketing user then verifies and publishes directly from the platform scheduler.
use_cases.justification: This directly addresses the pain point of manually copying approved content into each platform's scheduler. The tool reduces repetitive copy-paste work by auto-mapping content to platforms and pre-populating fields, leaving the user to verify and push the final publish button, maintaining human control.

criteria_rationale.quality_impact: Reduces transcription errors and ensures platform-guideline compliance, with minor consistency gain over manual scheduling.
criteria_rationale.strategic_alignment: Improves marketing team efficiency but is not tied to revenue or strategic growth.
criteria_rationale.data_quality: Approved content, platform guidelines, and scheduling systems are structured and readily available.
criteria_rationale.technical_complexity: Simple mapping and form-filling; native integrations already exist in most scheduling tools.
criteria_rationale.adoption_risk: No workflow disruption; the user still controls the final publish action.
criteria_rationale.off_the_shelf: Most commercial social media scheduling tools (Hootsuite, Buffer, Sprout Social) already offer content templating and multi-platform scheduling.
criteria_rationale.ai_act: No personal data processing, no profiling; internal content distribution is minimal risk.
criteria_rationale.gdpr: No personal data involved; only approved marketing content.

use_cases.description: A classifier that reads approval sign-offs and content metadata and auto-categorizes posts as 'ready to schedule', 'pending approval', 'revisions needed', or 'approved but awaiting asset', enabling the marketing team to filter and prioritize their calendar view without manual status updates.
use_cases.justification: This addresses the pain point of tracking which posts are pending versus published across multiple stakeholders and approval workflows. By automating status classification, it eliminates manual status-entry work and gives the team a real-time view of bottlenecks.

criteria_rationale.quality_impact: Eliminates manual status-logging errors; provides consistent, real-time classification across all posts.
criteria_rationale.strategic_alignment: Improves team coordination and calendar accuracy but not directly tied to company revenue or core strategy.
criteria_rationale.data_quality: Approval records and metadata exist but may be scattered across email, shared drives, and the calendar tool; moderate reliability.
criteria_rationale.technical_complexity: A lightweight classifier on structured fields (approval status, timestamps, asset flags); straightforward build.
criteria_rationale.adoption_risk: Minor workflow change; marketing team must trust the auto-classification and may need to override occasionally.
criteria_rationale.off_the_shelf: No existing off-the-shelf tool packages approval-workflow classification specifically for social media calendars.
criteria_rationale.ai_act: Internal content workflow automation with no profiling; minimal risk.
criteria_rationale.gdpr: No personal data processed; only content metadata and approval records.

use_cases.description: A classifier that reads incoming IT ticket descriptions and system logs, then assigns a severity level (critical, high, medium, low) and auto-populates the initial categorization based on the incident type and impact signals.
use_cases.justification: This directly addresses the pain point of inconsistent severity categorization on submission. By applying consistent criteria to every ticket (keywords, impact on systems, affected user count from logs), the classifier standardizes severity assignment and reduces downstream triage effort.

criteria_rationale.quality_impact: Applies severity rules consistently across all tickets, reducing missed critical issues and false escalations.
criteria_rationale.strategic_alignment: Improves incident response speed and prioritization, directly supporting operational reliability and SLA compliance.
criteria_rationale.data_quality: Ticket descriptions and system logs are already captured; structured fields exist for severity and category.
criteria_rationale.technical_complexity: Classification on text and log signals is a mature capability; standard ML models can be trained on historical ticket data.
criteria_rationale.adoption_risk: Ticket submitters see a pre-filled severity; support staff can override if needed. Minimal workflow disruption.
criteria_rationale.off_the_shelf: Ticket triage classifiers are common in ITSM platforms (Jira, ServiceNow integrations).
criteria_rationale.ai_act: Internal IT operations process with no profiling or decision-making about individuals.
criteria_rationale.gdpr: May indirectly reference employee names or departments in ticket text, but no sensitive personal data processing.

use_cases.description: An AI assistant that searches incident history, system logs, and ticket database for similar issues when a new ticket arrives, surfacing likely duplicates or related tickets to the on-call engineer for rapid routing decision.
use_cases.justification: This addresses the pain point that on-call engineers spend time figuring out ownership and that duplicate tickets go undetected. By automatically retrieving similar past incidents and their resolutions, the assistant enables faster routing and de-duplication without removing human judgment.

criteria_rationale.quality_impact: Reduces time spent searching history manually; human still validates the match and decides routing, so quality depends on retrieval relevance.
criteria_rationale.strategic_alignment: Reduces MTTR (mean time to resolution) and improves engineer efficiency, supporting operational reliability.
criteria_rationale.data_quality: Incident history, system logs, and ticket database are structured and available; searchability depends on data consistency.
criteria_rationale.technical_complexity: Semantic search / similarity matching on ticket text and logs is well-established; can use embeddings or keyword matching.
criteria_rationale.adoption_risk: Engineers still own the final routing decision; the tool is an advisory aid with minimal workflow change.
criteria_rationale.off_the_shelf: Ticket similarity and suggestion features are built into modern ITSM platforms.
criteria_rationale.ai_act: Information retrieval and routing aid; no autonomous action or profiling of individuals.
criteria_rationale.gdpr: Accesses ticket and incident history that may reference employee names or departments, but is not profiling or making automated decisions about individuals.

use_cases.description: A classifier that takes sales transactions and applies the complex commission rule set (by region, product line, and exception flags) to automatically categorize each transaction into the correct commission tier and rate.
use_cases.justification: This directly addresses the error-prone manual spreadsheet calculations and the complexity of applying many region/product-specific commission exceptions. By automating the rule application consistently, it reduces disputed calculations and frees time for handling edge cases and payroll integration.

criteria_rationale.quality_impact: Applies complex multi-factor rules consistently to every transaction, eliminating manual arithmetic errors and disputed calculations.
criteria_rationale.strategic_alignment: Directly supports cost control and payroll accuracy, critical operational priorities for a distribution company; also reduces rep friction from commission disputes.
criteria_rationale.data_quality: Sales transactions, territory assignments, and rule parameters are already structured and reliably captured in the ERP/payroll system.
criteria_rationale.technical_complexity: Requires encoding the region/product/exception rules as a decision tree or rule engine, then testing against historical data; moderate build effort.
criteria_rationale.adoption_risk: Sales ops team still validates and can override flagged outliers, so the workflow change is incremental rather than disruptive.
criteria_rationale.off_the_shelf: No out-of-the-box tool exists for this company's specific multi-dimensional commission rules; requires custom configuration.
criteria_rationale.ai_act: Internal payroll automation with no profiling or decision-making about individuals' behavior or performance is minimal risk.
criteria_rationale.gdpr: Processes employee sales and territory data (indirectly personal) but only for payroll calculation, not for profiling or evaluation.

use_cases.description: An AI tool that ingests employment contracts, ID documents, and tax forms from multiple submission channels, extracts key fields (name, role, start date, right-to-work status, tax details) and flags missing or incomplete documents.
use_cases.justification: This directly addresses the pain point of manual checking against a compliance checklist. By extracting and validating required fields consistently, it catches missing or incomplete documents early and reduces HR's manual review time.

criteria_rationale.quality_impact: Applies the compliance checklist consistently to every hire, catching missing documents and data inconsistencies that tired reviewers might miss.
criteria_rationale.strategic_alignment: Directly supports on-time system access and compliance, both key HR priorities.
criteria_rationale.data_quality: Documents vary in format and submission quality (images, PDFs, handwritten), but the required fields are present in most submissions.
criteria_rationale.technical_complexity: Multi-format document OCR plus field extraction from employment, tax, and ID documents is a well-established capability.
criteria_rationale.adoption_risk: HR still makes final decisions on document validity; the tool is an augmentation, not a full replacement.
criteria_rationale.off_the_shelf: Mature document extraction vendors already serve HR onboarding workflows.
criteria_rationale.ai_act: Internal HR process with no profiling of worker performance, behavior, or access decisions—minimal risk.
criteria_rationale.gdpr: Processes sensitive personal data including identity, tax, and right-to-work information, but only for administrative onboarding purposes.

use_cases.description: A classifier that reviews the extracted and validated documents and automatically flags onboarding cases as 'ready-for-provisioning', 'needs-review', or 'documents-missing', determining which new hires can proceed to IT system access.
use_cases.justification: This targets the pain point of delayed system access due to incomplete document review. By routing complete cases directly to IT provisioning and flagging exceptions, it accelerates the onboarding cycle and reduces HR bottleneck delays.

criteria_rationale.quality_impact: Applies triage rules consistently, reducing reviewer fatigue and human error on straightforward cases.
criteria_rationale.strategic_alignment: Directly reduces time-to-access and supports a smooth employee experience, a key HR priority.
criteria_rationale.data_quality: Operates on the structured, extracted fields from the first use case, ensuring consistent input.
criteria_rationale.technical_complexity: Simple rule-based or ML classification on a small set of structured attributes, low effort.
criteria_rationale.adoption_risk: HR retains final approval authority; the tool streamlines triage, not hiring decisions.
criteria_rationale.off_the_shelf: Workflow triage on structured data is a commodity capability, available in many HR automation platforms.
criteria_rationale.ai_act: Internal HR workflow routing with no behavioral profiling or hiring decisions—minimal risk.
criteria_rationale.gdpr: Uses the same sensitive personal data as the extraction step, in a non-discriminatory triage context.

use_cases.description: An AI tool that processes inspection photos and free-text notes to automatically extract and standardize hazard data into structured fields (hazard type, location, severity, root cause) aligned with the inspection checklist.
use_cases.justification: This directly addresses the inconsistency in inspector notes by applying a consistent extraction schema to every inspection. It converts unstructured free-text into machine-readable data that can then be queried, aggregated, and cross-referenced to identify recurring hazard patterns.

criteria_rationale.quality_impact: Standardizes data entry across inspectors, reducing omissions and inconsistencies that hamper hazard tracking.
criteria_rationale.strategic_alignment: Safety compliance and risk management are core to the sector and this company's operations; consistent hazard logging directly supports both.
criteria_rationale.data_quality: Inspection checklists are structured; site photos and notes are available but unstructured; existing incident history provides context.
criteria_rationale.technical_complexity: Combining OCR, photo analysis, and form field extraction is well-established; aligning to the company's checklist schema is moderately custom.
criteria_rationale.adoption_risk: Inspectors still fill out reports; the tool structures what they enter, so workflow change is minimal.
criteria_rationale.off_the_shelf: Several mature safety/compliance document extraction tools already handle this pattern.
criteria_rationale.ai_act: Internal safety inspection data processing with no profiling or decision-making on individuals; minimal risk.
criteria_rationale.gdpr: May indirectly reference employee or site-visitor names in notes, but the focus is on hazard data, not personal attributes.

use_cases.description: A classifier that flags corrective actions (from the logs) as on-track, overdue, or not-started based on the target close date and current status, surfacing untracked or stalled remediations without manual list checking.
use_cases.justification: This targets the pain point that corrective actions are not tracked to completion automatically. By classifying action status in real time, it ensures overdue remediation is visible immediately and raises accountability, reducing the manual effort to cross-reference logs and chase overdue items.

criteria_rationale.quality_impact: Automatic status tracking catches overdue actions that might be missed in a manually-checked log, improving closure rates.
criteria_rationale.strategic_alignment: Ensures corrective actions are completed on time, directly supporting compliance and safety risk reduction.
criteria_rationale.data_quality: Corrective action logs and target dates are already structured in the existing system; readily available.
criteria_rationale.technical_complexity: Simple date-based rule or lightweight classifier on structured fields; trivial to build and integrate.
criteria_rationale.adoption_risk: Automated alerts replace manual checks; minimal change to how safety teams work, mostly positive.
criteria_rationale.off_the_shelf: Status-based alert and triage is a commodity capability in most safety/compliance platforms.
criteria_rationale.ai_act: Internal tracking of remediation actions, no personal decision-making or profiling; minimal risk.
criteria_rationale.gdpr: Uses corrective action logs, which may reference responsible personnel indirectly, but is not profiling them.
